课程简介（中文）

本课程通过展现气候系统中若干重要现象，阐释动力学在气候变化与变异中的作用。这些现象包括季风、厄尔尼诺-南方涛动、马登-朱利安振荡、温盐环流及全球变暖。课程首先描述这些现象的观测特征，进而揭示其背后的关键过程，在阐述现象成因最新认知的同时，也指明当前存在的未解之谜。课程旨在帮助学生理解气候系统为何在变化以及未来可能会如何演变。

课程简介（英文）

This course illuminates the role of dynamics in climate change and variability through presenting some major climate phenomena in the climate system. These phenomena include monsoons, the El Niño-Southern Oscillation, the Madden-Julian Oscillation, the Pacific Decadal Oscillation, thermohaline circulation, and global warming. Observed characteristics of these phenomena are first described. Key processes behind them are then exposed. The state-of-the-art understanding of why these phenomena take place is provided, together with the known unknowns. Along the way, some key mathematical tools are introduced with the aim to better equip the students in their own pursuit of a deeper understanding of why the state of the climate system has varied in the way we have observed, and how it may change in the future.

教学目标

（Including value, knowledge and ability objectives）

At the end of the course, the students will be able to

  • Describe the machinery of the climate system: basic components of the system, interactions among the components, fundamental forces, and major circulations systems;
  • Describe climate phenomena introduced in the class including their spatial and temporal characteristics;
  • Name the major processes/forces behind these phenomena;
  • Explain why these climate phenomena take place;
  • Analyze existing theories for these climate phenomena and formulate their own research questions;
  • Apply their knowledge and understanding of these phenomena to explain or attribute the cause for a particular observed climate condition;
  • Formulate a conceptual model for why the state of the climate system has changed the way we have observed.

教学方式

This course employs traditional teaching methods, including lectures, classroom discussions, and group work. Additionally, we also incorporate innovative approaches such as the Socratic Method, which involves asking thought-provoking questions to stimulate critical thinking and deepen students' understanding. This combination of instructional techniques provides a well-rounded and adaptable learning experience, catering to diverse learning styles and fostering a deeper comprehension of the subject matter.

教学内容与进度安排

Week 1: Introduction and Overview of the Climate System: Goals, Approaches, and Road Maps (Yue Zhang)

Objectives:

  • Review the syllabus and understand the course mechanics
  • Recognize the structure, assignments, and schedule of this course as written in the syllabus
  • Inform the instructor what you particularly like to learn from this course
  • Describe each component of the Earth's climate system
  • Describe how these components interact with each other

Weeks 2-3: The Climate System: Components, Interactions, Forces, and Circulations (Yue Zhang)

Objectives:

  • Describe the main energy source and sink of the Earth's climate system
  • Identify the main forces that set the atmosphere and ocean in motion
  • Name the major circulation systems in the atmosphere and the ocean

Weeks 4-5: Monsoons: A Seasonal Dialogue Between the Land and the Adjacent Oceans (Yue Zhang)

Objectives:

  • Identify the cause of seasons
  • Describe the differences in the response to solar heating between the land and the ocean
  • Describe the characteristics of monsoons
  • Understand the fundamental characteristics of the Indian monsoon, East Asian monsoon, African monsoon, and North American monsoon
  • Identify and describe the key processes involved in the life cycles of the aforementioned monsoon systems
  • Explain why there are monsoons

Weeks 6-7: The El Niño-Southern Oscillation (ENSO): Coupling between the Atmosphere and the Ocean (Yue Zhang)

Objectives:

  • Describe the basic characteristics of tropical sea surface temperature (SST) and rainfall distributions
  • Name the tropical Pacific warm pool and the tropical Pacific cold-tongue
  • Name the major circulations in the atmosphere and in the ocean over the tropical Pacific region
  • Name the exchange processes between the atmosphere and ocean
  • Describe the responses of the tropical atmosphere to changes in SSTs
  • Describe the responses of the tropical ocean to changes in zonal winds
  • Define what is the Bjerknes feedback

Week 8: Interannual Ocean-Atmosphere Coupled Oscillations in the Tropical Indian and Atlantic Oceans (Yue Zhang)

Objectives:

  • Explain the basic characteristics of interannual SST variability in the tropical Indian and Atlantic oceans, analogous to ENSO in the tropical Pacific
  • Identify the major atmospheric and oceanic processes involved in the Indian Ocean Dipole (IOD) and the Atlantic Niño
  • Describe the role of SST anomalies in driving atmospheric convection and circulation changes in these regions
  • Understand the feedback mechanisms that sustain these oscillations
  • Discuss the differences and similarities between ENSO, the IOD, and the Atlantic Niño in terms of their life cycles and teleconnections

Weeks 9-10: The Madden-Julian Oscillation (MJO): Organization of Weather Events Over the Warm Oceans (Wei Mei)

Objectives:

  • Name three different forms of heat transfer
  • Name the function and the driving force of deep convection in the tropical atmosphere
  • Describe the spatial and temporal characteristics of the MJO
  • Name the physical processes that are involved in the formation of the MJO
  • Understand why there is the MJO

Week 11: The Pacific Decadal Oscillation (PDO): Ocean-Atmosphere Climate Variability Centered over the Mid-latitude Pacific Basin (Wei Mei)

Objectives:

  • Describe the characteristics of the PDO
  • Contrast the PDO with ENSO
  • Name the atmospheric "bridge" and describe the role of the atmospheric "bridge" in connecting the tropics and extra-tropics
  • Explain the PDO as the sum of several processes with different dynamic origins

Week 12: Thermohaline Circulation: Making the Earth’s Oceans a Global System (Wei Mei)

Objectives:

  • Describe the structure of the thermohaline circulation
  • Name the primary regions of deep water formation and describe the processes of deep water formation
  • Understand why there is thermohaline circulation and describe its impacts
  • Define what is a tipping point

Week 13: Paleoclimatology: Reconstructing Ancient Climates (Wei Mei)

Objectives:

  • Name major proxies for climate
  • Name notable climate events in Earth history
  • Describe climate during geological ages
  • Understand underlying internal and external forcings

Weeks 14-15: Global Warming: Observations, Theories, and the Science and Art of Modeling (Wei Mei)

Objectives:

  • Describe the temporal and spatial characteristics of global warming
  • Describe radiative forcing from CO2 and other man-made greenhouse gases
  • Describe the water vapor feedback, ice albedo feedback, and other important or potentially important radiative feedbacks
  • Describe the role of the ocean
  • Describe the successes and failures of the state-of-the-art climate models in simulating the recent global warming

Week 16: Presentation (Wei Mei)
